Create a NICHESObject from Single-Cell Data

Source: R/create_NICHESObject.R
create_NICHESObject.Rd

The primary entry point for NICHESv2. Supports two analysis modes:

"spatial"

Edges defined by physical proximity using kNN or radius in x/y space. Requires x and y in meta.data.

"nonspatial"

NICHES v1-style type-stratified sampling. Requires cell.type.col.

Usage

create_NICHESObject(
  count.mtx,
  meta.data,
  LRM.db,
  mode = c("spatial", "nonspatial"),
  species = "human",
  sample.col = NULL,
  cell.type.col = NULL,
  ligand.col = "ligand",
  receptor.col = "receptor",
  k = NULL,
  rad = NULL,
  seed = 42L,
  max.cells = NULL,
  method = c("product", "minimum"),
  normalize.method = c("prop", "none"),
  gene.meta = NULL,
  n.cores = 1L,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

count.mtx

Gene x cell matrix (sparse dgCMatrix or dense). Row names = gene symbols; column names = cell barcodes. Both name sets must match rownames(meta.data) and the columns of LRM.db respectively.

meta.data

data.frame with row names = cell barcodes. Must contain x and y columns when mode = "spatial", and the column named by cell.type.col when mode = "nonspatial".

LRM.db

Either a character string naming a built-in database ("connectomedb2025", "fantom5" or "omnipath") or a data.frame with at least the columns named by ligand.col and receptor.col. See load_LRM_database for details and supported species.

mode

Character. "spatial" (default, kNN/radius edges) or "nonspatial" (type-stratified random sampling).

species

Species for built-in LRM databases. One of "human" (default), "mouse", "rat", or "pig" ("pig" is not available from OmniPath). Silently ignored when LRM.db is a data.frame.

sample.col

Character or NULL (default). Name of a column in meta.data identifying the biological sample of origin for each cell. When supplied, the pipeline runs independently within each sample and the per-sample objects are merged. See the Sample-aware processing section above for the barcode-uniqueness requirement.

cell.type.col

Character or NULL. Column in meta.data holding cell type labels. Required for mode = "nonspatial"; ignored otherwise.

ligand.col

Character. Column name for ligands in LRM.db. Default "ligand".

receptor.col

Character. Column name for receptors in LRM.db. Default "receptor".

k

Integer or NULL. Number of nearest neighbors for kNN edges. Spatial mode only; supply exactly one of k or rad.

rad

Numeric or NULL. Neighborhood radius for fixed-radius edges (same units as the x/y columns). Spatial mode only; supply exactly one of k or rad. Use Explore_Radius_Neighborhood to choose a sensible value.

seed

Integer. Random seed for reproducible type-stratified sampling. Default 42L. Nonspatial mode only.

max.cells

Integer or NULL. Per cell-type-pair edge cap. Default NULL (no cap). Nonspatial mode only.

method

Per-edge LR scoring method. "product" (default) multiplies sender ligand expression by receiver receptor expression; "minimum" takes the elementwise minimum. Both handle gene complexes (underscore-joined symbols).

normalize.method

Edge-level normalization for score.norm in $edge.data. "prop" (default) scales each edge's per-LRM scores to sum to 1 across LRMs; "none" leaves score.norm equal to score.

gene.meta

Optional data.frame with a "gene" column (and any number of additional annotation columns) joined onto the $gene.meta slot. Default NULL.

n.cores

Integer. Number of CPU cores for the inner scoring pipeline. Default 1L. Always uses socket clusters (parallel::makeCluster) for cross-platform compatibility.

verbose

Logical. Print progress messages. Default TRUE.

Value

A NICHESObject with attribute "mode" set to either "spatial" or "nonspatial". When sample.col is provided, attribute "sample.col" is also set to the column name. Slots $cell.list, $cell.data, $cell.meta, $edge.list, $edge.data, $edge.meta, $gene.list, $gene.meta, $LRM.list, and $LRM.meta are always populated. The three neighborhood slots are always populated and attr(obj, "edge.filter.mode") and attr(obj, "remove.autocrine") are set on the object. $segmentation always remains NULL until add_segmentation is called.

Pipeline overview

Internally, create_NICHESObject() chains the following steps:

  1. Load the LR database (load_LRM_database) when LRM.db is a character string; otherwise the supplied data.frame is used directly.

  2. Build the edge list – create_Edgelist_Spatial for mode = "spatial" or create_Edgelist_SamplingByType for mode = "nonspatial".

  3. Score every edge x LRM combination via compute_CellToCell, sparsifying as it goes.

  4. Assemble the 15-slot NICHESObject (cell, edge, gene, LRM, segmentation, and aggregation slots).

  5. Extract neighborhoods via add_neighborhoods using edge.filter.mode = "both_in_neighborhood" and remove.autocrine = FALSE (fixed by design).

Each step is also exported individually for users who need finer control.

Sample-aware processing

When sample.col is supplied, meta.data is split by that column and the full pipeline runs independently within each sample. Per-sample objects are then combined via merge_NICHESObjects. This prevents physically meaningless cross-sample edges (a kNN search on coordinates pooled across slides will happily connect cells that were never on the same tissue).

Barcodes must be globally unique across samples. A duplicate barcode is a hard error during the merge step. Prepend a sample-specific prefix before construction (e.g.\ paste0(sample.id, "_", barcode), which is what Seurat::RenameCells() does automatically).

Outer iteration over samples is always sequential; the inner pipeline uses n.cores for parallelism, so socket clusters are never nested.

See also

NICHESv2_example for an example object produced by this function; merge_NICHESObjects for combining objects produced independently; compute_CellToCell for the underlying scoring engine; create_Edgelist_Spatial, create_Edgelist_SamplingByType for the edge-list constructors invoked internally; load_LRM_database for the LR-database loader; aggregate_NICHESObject for downstream summarization.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(NICHESv2_inputs)

# ---- Basic spatial mode (kNN edges) ----
obj <- create_NICHESObject(
  count.mtx    = NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx,
  meta.data    = NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data,
  LRM.db       = NICHESv2_inputs$LRM.db,
  mode         = "spatial",
  ligand.col   = "ligand",
  receptor.col = "receptor",
  k            = 5L,
  n.cores      = 1L,
  verbose      = FALSE
)
#> [create_Edgelist_Spatial] Mode: kNN    | Param: 5 | Cells: 80 | Inter-cell: 274 | Autocrine: 80
#> [compute_CellToCell] 354 edges x 15 LR pairs | method = 'product' | cores = 1
#> [compute_CellToCell] Done. 190 non-zero edge signals.
print(obj)
#> -- NICHESObject --------------------------------------------
#>   Cells        : 80  (80 non-empty)
#>   Genes        : 50  (50 valid)
#>   Edges        : 354  (141 non-empty)
#>   LRM pairs    : 15  (15 valid)
#>   Segmentation : none
#>   Neighborhoods: 80 cells  |  1364 edges  (mode: both_in_neighborhood, autocrine: included)
#>   Aggregations : none
#> 
#>   Slot summary:
#>     $cell.list     -- character vector of cell barcodes
#>     $cell.data     -- (cell, gene, score, score.norm) [sparse]
#>     $cell.meta     -- per-cell metadata
#>     $edge.list     -- (edge, SendingCell, ReceivingCell)
#>     $edge.data     -- (edge, LRM, score, score.norm) [sparse]
#>     $edge.meta     -- per-edge metadata with Sending/Receiving/Joint cols
#>     $neighborhood.cell.list -- named list: cell -> neighbor barcodes
#>     $neighborhood.edge.list -- named list: cell -> edge IDs
#>     $neighborhood.meta      -- (cell, n.neighbors, n.edges) [keyed]
#>     $gene.list     -- character vector of gene names
#>     $gene.meta     -- per-gene metadata
#>     $LRM.list      -- character vector of 'ligand|receptor' pairs
#>     $LRM.meta      -- per-LRM metadata
#>     $segmentation  -- sf object of cell polygons, or NULL
#>     $aggregations  -- named list of aggregation data.tables
#> ------------------------------------------------------------
attr(obj, "mode")           # "spatial"
#> [1] "spatial"

# ---- Nonspatial mode (NICHES v1-style type-stratified sampling) ----
obj.sampled <- create_NICHESObject(
  count.mtx     = NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx,
  meta.data     = NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data,
  LRM.db        = NICHESv2_inputs$LRM.db,
  mode          = "nonspatial",
  cell.type.col = "celltype",
  ligand.col    = "ligand",
  receptor.col  = "receptor",
  n.cores       = 1L,
  verbose       = FALSE
)
#> [create_Edgelist_SamplingByType] 3 cell types | seed = 42 | max.cells = none | 230 sampled directed edges.
#> [compute_CellToCell] 230 edges x 15 LR pairs | method = 'product' | cores = 1
#> [compute_CellToCell] Done. 123 non-zero edge signals.
attr(obj.sampled, "mode")   # "nonspatial"
#> [1] "nonspatial"

# ---- Sample-aware processing (sample.col) ----
# Synthesise a 'sample' column to demonstrate the split-and-merge path.
# Real workflows: ensure barcodes are globally unique across samples.
md <- NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data
md$sample <- rep(c("S1", "S2"), each = nrow(md) / 2L)

obj.split <- create_NICHESObject(
  count.mtx    = NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx,
  meta.data    = md,
  LRM.db       = NICHESv2_inputs$LRM.db,
  mode         = "spatial",
  sample.col   = "sample",
  ligand.col   = "ligand",
  receptor.col = "receptor",
  k            = 5L,
  n.cores      = 1L,
  verbose      = FALSE
)
#> [create_Edgelist_Spatial] Mode: kNN    | Param: 5 | Cells: 40 | Inter-cell: 142 | Autocrine: 40
#> [compute_CellToCell] 182 edges x 15 LR pairs | method = 'product' | cores = 1
#> [compute_CellToCell] Done. 113 non-zero edge signals.
#> [create_Edgelist_Spatial] Mode: kNN    | Param: 5 | Cells: 40 | Inter-cell: 146 | Autocrine: 40
#> [compute_CellToCell] 186 edges x 15 LR pairs | method = 'product' | cores = 1
#> [compute_CellToCell] Done. 80 non-zero edge signals.
attr(obj.split, "sample.col")   # "sample"
#> [1] "sample"
# }
